analysis.title: Groupon Inc. (GRPN) Q3'26 Review: Near-Term Headwinds Build & Result in Reduced Guidance; Investor Focus Likely Shifts Towards 2027 Trajectory
key_insights: GS maintains Sell on Groupon and cuts its 12-month price target from $16 to $11. With the price at $16.25, that implies 32.3% downside.

Q3'26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA missed the guidance range, GS and consensus. Management cited lower take rates, Trust & Quality investments and higher marketing spend at lower-than-expected returns.
Q3 gross billings grew 6% YoY to $439M, near the high end of guidance. Things to Do, Travel and International Local drove it, and North America Local returned to growth at +4% billings.
Core Local supply, including Small Business and Health, Beauty & Wellness, remains a focus. Management expects benefits from the supply rebuild to begin showing in 2027.

Customer engagement is weak. Active customers were flat at 16.2M, as double-digit new customer growth was offset by lower purchase frequency and more one-time customers. Management is shifting its acquisition framework from near-term transaction ROI toward customer LTV.
Trust & Quality investments were a ~180bps headwind to Q3 billings growth, and management expects the investment to continue.
Management lowered FY26 guidance on weaker marketing returns, lower take rates, Trust & Quality headwinds and slower progress on Customer Lifecycle initiatives.
GS cuts Q4'26 estimates: gross billings $474M (from $486M), revenue $135M (from $147M), adjusted EBITDA $20M (from $30M).
GS cuts 2027 estimates: gross billings $1.77B (from $1.79B), revenue $522M (from $544M), adjusted EBITDA $70M (from $92M). Take rate estimates fall about 80-100bps across 2026-2028.

AI is a stated efficiency lever (Project Foundry). AI resolves more than 90% of customer support contacts as of early November, revenue per employee is up 50% YoY, and the LivingSocial relaunch is an early agentic commerce effort.
Capital return continues: $11.3M of shares repurchased since the prior earnings release, $43M year to date, with $202M remaining under the authorization.

GS expects near-term investor focus on stabilizing North America Core Local supply, improving returns on marketing spend, and showing that Trust & Quality and Customer Lifecycle investments lift frequency and contribution profit. The longer-term debate is whether these and AI efficiencies support durable billings and earnings growth in 2027 and beyond.

market_movers.rationale: Sell maintained, price target cut from $16 to $11 on lower forward estimates after the Q3'26 miss and reduced guidance. GS sees risk-reward skewing more negatively relative to its coverage universe.

earnings_insights: Q3'26 revenue reported $125M vs GS est $129M and consensus est $129M, below the company guide of $128-130M.
Q3'26 adjusted EBITDA reported $15M vs GS est $19M and consensus est $20M, below the company guide of $19-21M. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 11.7% vs GS est 15%.
Q3'26 GAAP operating income reported $4M vs GS est $3M and consensus est $1M. Free cash flow reported -$46M vs GS est -$14M and consensus est -$3M.
Q3'26 gross billings reported +6% YoY to $439M. North America billings +4% YoY. Active customers flat at 16.2M.

GS FY26E revenue $502M (from $519M), adjusted EBITDA $63M (from $77M), GAAP operating income $3M (from $11M). FY27E revenue $522M (from $544M), adjusted EBITDA $70M (from $92M). All are GS estimates, not reported figures.
GS EPS estimates (diluted, pre-exceptional): FY26E -$0.38 (from -$0.13), FY27E $0.25 (from $0.56), FY28E $0.41 (from $0.72). FY25 reported -$1.87.
risk_factors: Risks to the Sell rating: Local billings and revenue growth above GS estimates, especially with faster user growth than expected.
Greater merchant adoption of the company's products.
Groupon could be acquired by another company (GS M&A rank is 3, low probability, 0%-15%).
Any moderation of the competitive environment, such as Google and Yelp.
Better-than-expected macro environment and consumer spending trends.

tension_points.bull_case: North America Local returned to growth (+4% billings) on Things to Do strength. Management expects benefits from the Core Local supply rebuild to begin showing in 2027, and AI efficiencies (revenue per employee +50% YoY) could support earnings growth. GS's upside scenario value is $21.
tension_points.bear_case: Q3 revenue and adjusted EBITDA missed on lower take rates and marketing spend at weak returns. Active customers are flat at 16.2M with falling purchase frequency and more one-time customers. FY26 guidance was lowered, and GS cuts 2027 adjusted EBITDA to $70mm from $92mm.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Local billings and revenue growth above GS estimates, especially if supported by faster user growth than expected.

theme_stances.key_argument: Near-term headwinds from lower take rates, Trust & Quality costs and weak marketing returns lead GS to cut estimates and keep risk-reward skewed negatively.
